table.name: Load Estimate Hold - Activation Load
RPM

table.description:
Load above which the higher filtered load estimate can be held. Other activation and release conditions apply.

table.name: BCS Correction Mode
table.description: Engine load (0) corrects boost-solenoid duty using the difference between actual and target engine load, with overboost correction when its pressure limit is exceeded. Boost pressure (1, or any nonzero value) uses the difference between actual and target pressure. This selection does not enable the separate alternate targeting strategy.

table.name: BCS DC Accumulated Correction Limit - Decrease
table.description:
Limits accumulated duty reduction. More negative values allow more reduction. Overall correction and final duty limits still apply.
Values are percentage points of commanded duty: +5 changes a 40% duty request to 45% before later limits. This is not a 5% multiplier.

table.name: BCS DC Accumulated Correction Limit - Increase
table.description:
Limits accumulated duty increase. Raising this value allows more accumulated positive correction. Overall correction and final duty limits still apply.
Values are percentage points of commanded duty: +5 changes a 40% duty request to 45% before later limits. This is not a 5% multiplier.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment - Boost Limit Exceeded
Pressure Above Overboost Limit (psi)

table.description:
Added to accumulated duty correction each update while overboost is latched in load-error mode. Positive values add duty; negative values subtract duty. Correction limits apply. Values beyond an axis use its nearest endpoint.
Values are percentage points of commanded duty: +5 changes a 40% duty request to 45% before later limits. This is not a 5% multiplier.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Barometer
Barometric Pressure (psi absolute)

table.description:
Scales base duty with barometric pressure. 100% leaves base duty unchanged; lower values reduce it and higher values increase it. Values beyond an axis use its nearest endpoint.
Values are percent of base duty: 100 leaves it unchanged; 90 applies 90% of the base request.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Battery Voltage
Battery Volts (V)

table.description:
Adds duty points for battery-voltage compensation. Positive values increase commanded duty; negative values reduce it. Final duty limits apply. Values beyond an axis use its nearest endpoint.
Values are percentage points of commanded duty: +5 changes a 40% duty request to 45% before later limits. This is not a 5% multiplier.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Boost Target Correction (Boost Targeting Mode)
Actual Pressure - Target Pressure (psi)

table.description:
Accumulated duty-point correction from actual pressure minus target pressure. Used when BCS Correction Mode is nonzero. Positive values add duty; negative values subtract duty. Correction and final-duty limits apply. Values beyond an axis use its nearest endpoint.
Values are percentage points of commanded duty: +5 changes a 40% duty request to 45% before later limits. This is not a 5% multiplier.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment IAT
Intake Air Temperature (degF)

table.description:
Scales base duty with intake air temperature. 100% leaves base duty unchanged; lower values reduce it and higher values increase it. Values beyond an axis use its nearest endpoint.
Values are percent of base duty: 100 leaves it unchanged; 90 applies 90% of the base request.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Limit - Decrease
table.description:
Lower limit on the initial plus accumulated duty correction. The accumulated correction also has its own limit; final duty remains within 0 to 100 percent.
Values are percentage points of commanded duty: +5 changes a 40% duty request to 45% before later limits. This is not a 5% multiplier.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Limit - Increase
table.description:
Upper limit on the initial plus accumulated duty correction. The accumulated correction also has its own limit; final duty remains within 0 to 100 percent.
Values are percentage points of commanded duty: +5 changes a 40% duty request to 45% before later limits. This is not a 5% multiplier.

table.name: BCS DC Base
RPM
Throttle Input (%)

table.description:
Base wastegate solenoid duty by RPM and selected throttle input. Higher values increase commanded duty before multipliers, corrections and limits. Values beyond an axis use its nearest endpoint.
Values are solenoid duty percent on a 0–100 scale. Commanded duty is not a measured boost-pressure target.

table.name: BCS Throttle Input
table.description: 0 uses measured throttle position for the wastegate lookup. Any nonzero value uses the throttle target from the active normal or alternate strategy. The selected input is limited by the lookup axis.

table.name: Boost Limit Barometer Adjustment
RPM
Barometric Pressure (PSI)

table.description: Scales the base overboost pressure limit by RPM and barometric pressure. 100% leaves the base limit unchanged; 90% lowers it by 10%; 110% raises it by 10%. This changes the pressure limit used by overboost correction, not its duty-cycle adjustment.

table.name: Overboost Pressure Limit - Base
RPM

table.description:
Base pressure limit for overboost correction. Barometric adjustment scales the limit; hysteresis controls when correction clears.
Values are absolute pressure and include atmospheric pressure; they are not gauge boost. Gauge boost is absolute pressure minus current barometric pressure.

table.name: Overboost Pressure Limit Hysteresis

Load

table.name: Cold Cranking and Afterstart Enrichment Decrement
Engine Coolant Temperature (°F)

table.name: Conditional Fuel Correction - RPM Factor
Engine Speed (RPM)

table.description: One factor in a conditional fuel correction: coolant factor × RPM factor × signal-ratio factor. table.name: Fuel Feedback Gain
Airflow (g/s)

table.description: Dimensionless gain for the fuel-feedback controller at each airflow. table.name: Fuel Feedback Response Period
Airflow (g/s)

table.description: Response period in seconds used with Fuel Feedback Gain to calculate controller coefficients. Increasing it reduces the integral coefficient magnitude and increases the derivative coefficient magnitude. This is a controller tuning period, not a logging interval or a guaranteed sensor delay. Values beyond an axis use its nearest endpoint.

table.name: Fuel Specific Gravity
table.description: Fuel-density coefficient used to convert requested fuel quantity into fuel volume. Keep it positive. The existing values are preserved without a unit conversion. table.name: Load Change Fuel Correction - Drop Amount
Coolant Temperature (°F)

table.description: Load-drop fuel correction in percentage points. Larger values request a larger correction when this path is enabled. table.name: Load Change Fuel Correction - Rise Offset
